source_policy: Preloaded scope references checked 2026-10-01; no automatic update, installation, model call or backend execution. Retrieval does not establish applicability or scientific success.

cards.title: Contraction and target bias
conditions: The exported update is exactly a finite rational affine map on the declared domain.
The target and infinity norm are specified independently of observed convergence.
cards.diagnostic: Use affine_dynamics to check the induced infinity norm and target fixed-point residual separately. A contracting map may converge to a biased fixed point; failure of this norm bound does not imply divergence.
limitations: This bounded verifier does not certify arbitrary nonlinear or learned dynamics.
Contraction is sufficient under its stated assumptions, not necessary for convergence or task utility.

cards.title: Local spectrum and transient growth
conditions: A finite Jacobian of the specified discrete update is available with its evaluation point.
For equilibrium stability reasoning, first verify the point is an equilibrium and check regularity assumptions.
cards.diagnostic: Compare spectral radius and largest singular value in the snapshot probe. A nonnormal matrix can amplify perturbations transiently despite spectral radius below one; seek a declared-domain bound when the local/global gap matters.
limitations: A local radius above one away from equilibrium does not establish a limit cycle or global divergence.
The numeric snapshot does not certify stability, Jacobian correctness or task gain; continuous-time generators need different stability criteria.

prerequisites: NumPy available in the execution environment
finite bounded exported matrix and source scope

cards.title: State-space and horizon refinement
conditions: Compare a stated state-space or iterative update at the same horizon, input and initial condition.
State the discretization rule and keep step count separate from model capacity.
cards.diagnostic: Use fixed-horizon refinement differences to decide whether numerical step sensitivity warrants a discretization study before an architecture change. A state-space formulation is a general route; Mamba is one selective state-space architecture, not the parent of every state-space model.
limitations: Finite refinement differences do not prove a continuum limit or resolution invariance.
This card neither recommends Mamba automatically nor supplies a task-gain guarantee.

prerequisites: explicit shared horizon and source scope

cards.title: Residual subspace and HAVOK
conditions: Residuals use a declared alignment, scale and sample scope.
A delay-coordinate/HAVOK study additionally needs a sampled time series and explicit embedding choices.
cards.diagnostic: First measure residual energy concentration with the snapshot SVD. If structure survives held-out samples, consider a separately budgeted PyDMD HAVOK study of delay coordinates and linear dynamics with forcing.
limitations: Residual rank or energy concentration does not identify minimal hidden-state dimension.
HAVOK fitting is not implemented by the snapshot SVD and does not establish causality or a universal Koopman representation.

prerequisites: separate PyDMD environment and authorized fit budget for HAVOK

cards.title: Exact proof and dimension constraints
conditions: Express the obligation in an existing registered finite schema instead of treating a symbolic fit as proof.
Separate tensor shape compatibility from physical units; physical dimensional analysis still needs an explicit domain specification.
cards.diagnostic: Use registered exact tensor identities/bounds, affine checks or supported rational obligations to find a concrete incompatibility or replayable certificate. Native Lean obligations require an available Lean backend for LEAN_KERNEL_CHECKED assurance.
limitations: Finite rational checks are not a general symbolic algebra system or Lean kernel proof.
Shape compatibility is not physical dimensional consistency; unsupported claims remain UNKNOWN.

capability.backend: registered exact certificates; optional native Lean
prerequisites: rational data and supported expression operations
native Lean installation only for Lean kernel assurance

cards.title: Sparse equation discovery
conditions: A sparse representation in a specified function library is plausible.
State sampling, differentiation/noise handling and train/validation separation before fitting.
cards.diagnostic: An authorized PySINDy fit can test which sparse candidate equations predict held-out dynamics within the chosen library; compare library and noise sensitivity rather than declaring the recovered equation a law.
limitations: Sparse identification depends on the library, derivative estimates, data excitation and regularization.
A fitted equation is neither a causal identification result nor an exact proof.

cards.title: Symbolic regression candidates
conditions: An interpretable expression is useful and operator/complexity constraints can be specified.
Keep equation search and held-out evaluation distinct; encode domain or unit restrictions explicitly when needed.
cards.diagnostic: A separately authorized PySR search can supply expression candidates on a loss/complexity tradeoff for held-out testing or later exact verification.
limitations: Expression search does not prove uniqueness, causality or global validity.
PySR uses Julia; its first import can install dependencies, and fitting can launch Julia workers. This selector never imports it or provisions an environment.

prerequisites: separately provisioned PySR and Julia environment

cards.title: Actual entrypoint and shape preflight
conditions: Identify the actual model type and formal/sampler entrypoint rather than assuming another model's interface.
Use representative split, channel, tile and batch shapes; declare expected call and hook counts before checking.
cards.diagnostic: Use inspect.signature(callable).bind(*args, **kwargs) to detect argument-interface mismatches, then a project-specific checker with bounded actual calls to compare shapes and expected/observed entrypoint events. For PyTorch, invoking the module and invoking forward directly differ in hook handling; count the events on the actual sampler path.
limitations: Signature binding checks arguments, not tensor shapes, values or scientific correctness.
CPU checks do not establish CUDA behavior; exit zero does not establish output quality or task gain.
RDS has no universal model/geometry checker and does not automatically execute the model or launch GPU jobs.

capability.backend: Python signature inspection and project-specific bounded calls
capability.readiness_only: scripts/rds_capabilities.py probes one selected environment capability, not project interfaces or input geometry
prerequisites: project/domain adapter implementing explicit assertions and event counts
authorized execution budget and device scope; native RDS exec wrapper supplies receipts only

cards.title: Equivalence saturation and e-graph term rewriting
conditions: Equational theories with non-directional rewrite rules (such as commutativity and associativity).
Saturation uses bounded iteration and e-node limits before extraction.
cards.diagnostic: Use equality saturation via E-Graphs (egglog/egg) to discover algebraically equivalent canonical expressions without phase-ordering divergence. Traditional rewriting cycles under AC-rules, whereas e-graphs compactly represent exponentially many equivalent terms.
limitations: Equivalence saturation is incomplete if iteration or term node limits are exhausted.
An algebraic term equivalence does not establish physical dimensional validity or empirical task gain.

capability.backend: Rust egglog or native E-Graph operator
prerequisites: Python egglog package or native Rust egg engine

cards.title: Lean axiom and environment audit
conditions: The proposition is expressed in supported closed syntax or registered statement schema.
Allowed axioms (e.g. empty set for constructive/computable arithmetic, or standard classical axioms) are explicitly declared.
cards.diagnostic: Review actual Lean axioms via #print axioms or native Lean audit. If proof depends on disallowed axioms (e.g. Classical.choice, propext, or sorry), refuse promotion; surface missing premises or seek axiom-free constructive reduction.
limitations: Axiom audit verifies formal dependency of the encoded theorem, not correspondence to physical reality or empirical task success.
Missing Lean toolchain falls back to deterministic AST parser audit.

capability.backend: Lean 4 #print axioms audit with safe AST parser fallback

cards.title: Bounded finite model and counterexample search
required_inputs: operation Cayley table or algebraic law
conditions: The domain is finite and explicitly bounded (e.g. small group Z_n, S_n, or finite algebraic structure).
Conjecture predicate is decidable on all elements in the bounded domain.
cards.diagnostic: Exhaustively checks conjecture over all domain elements or Cayley table tuples. If violation found, produces minimal reproducible counterexample witness to refute the unbounded or general claim; if all pass, certifies bounded property without claiming universal unconstrained theorem.
limitations: Bounded finite verification does not prove universal claims on infinite domains.
Small-order verification cannot rule out asymptotic or large-cardinality counterexamples.

capability.backend: pure-Python exhaustive finite domain search and Cayley table checker

cards.title: Explicit reduction and representation transfer
conditions: Explicit mapping f: Source -> Target and reconstruction g: Target -> Source.
Preservation of solution/validity equivalence: Valid(x) iff Valid(f(x)).
cards.diagnostic: Checks that reduction preserves exact semantics and bounds on sample instances. Tracks open transfer obligations (e.g., unproved backward implication or domain constraint mismatch) so that unclosed transfer does not masquerade as a solved theorem.
limitations: Verifying finite sample instances of a reduction does not prove correctness of the reduction in full generality.
Translating a problem to another domain does not guarantee computational tractability.

capability.backend: symbolic reduction mapping validator and certificate transport
